title: Overdrive Domination Gameplay!
author: ProfMags
selftext:
Hello everyone! I wanted to show off a new game mode I've recently added to my Transformers inspired game, OverDrive!

This is Domination, heavily inspired by Call of Duty. The objective is to capture and hold three rotating points around the map while fighting against the enemy team. The mode also features scorestreaks, and players can choose between different classes, each with their own unique stats and abilities that offer different but balanced playstyles.

In a recent update, I also completely overhauled the weapon system, allowing players to customize their weapons with different attachments. Each attachment affects the weapon's stats, so players can build their loadouts around their preferred playstyle.

I've also taken the feedback from my last post into consideration and made some improvements to the game's visuals, particularly the lighting. I've significantly improved the overall lighting and gotten rid of the excessive bloom that a few people pointed out. I really appreciate everyone who took the time to give feedback, as it's genuinely helping me improve the game!

I've been putting a ton of time into developing and improving OverDrive, and it's been really exciting seeing everything come together!

For those curious about the development process, I've been using Opus 5.5 for the VFX and most of the environmental assets, while Tripo was used to generate the character models. All of the core gameplay systems, mechanics, and overall game design were designed and implemented by me.

I hope you guys enjoy this little showcase! I'd love to hear what everyone thinks, and any feedback or suggestions are always appreciated!

comments.author: Timely-Tradition-471
comments.body:
OverDrive looks like it’s coming together nicely! The Domination mode and weapon attachments sound like they add a lot of replayability, and I think it’s great that you’ve been taking community feedback and using it to improve the visuals. It’s always interesting to see how an indie project develops as more systems come together.

I’m Josh, part of the Tripo Studio team on the U.S. side. I’d love to connect and learn more about your development process, especially how you’ve been incorporating Tripo character models into the game. Are you planning to expand the roster of playable Transformers or focus on refining the existing gameplay modes next?
